Solutions/Pallet storage

Drive-In / Drive-Through Racking

Deep-lane pallet storage for batches of similar products.

Discuss this system → Read the FAQs ↓

Overview

How it works

Drive-in and drive-through layouts prioritise high storage density through deep pallet lanes. Forklifts enter or service the rack lanes, so pallet rotation, protective systems and operating discipline are central design decisions.

Typical applications

  • Cold storage
  • Bulk seasonal products
  • Large consistent pallet batches

Benefits

Why choose it

01

Dense batch storage

Useful for many pallets of the same SKU or similar stock.

02

Reduced aisle share

More floor space can be dedicated to rack lanes.

03

Rotation choices

Different lane arrangements can support different stock-management approaches.

Engineering

Design considerations

Lane depth
Based on batch quantities, pallet type and forklift constraints.
Stock rotation
Drive-in typically LIFO; drive-through can support FIFO layouts.
Forklift clearance
Engineered for truck envelope and operating tolerances.
Protective features
Guide rails, upright protection and controlled entry.
Load capacity
Determined by the approved rack and foundation design.

Technical specifications are design considerations, not fixed certified performance values. Confirm claims with engineering and supplier data before deployment.

FAQs

Common questions

What is the difference between drive-in and drive-through?

Drive-in generally loads and unloads from one end, often favouring LIFO rotation. Drive-through has access from opposite ends and can support FIFO workflows.

Is drive-in suitable for many different SKUs?

It is usually better suited to fewer SKUs held in larger pallet batches, because deep lanes limit access to individual loads.

What operating risks need attention?

Truck entry clearances, rack impact protection, trained operators, load compatibility and disciplined lane management are important.

How is lane depth selected?

Engineers balance stock batch quantity, load dimensions, building space, safe access and replenishment patterns.
